chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Al-Mukhtar, from Abdullah ibn Abu Yafour, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Be patient and excel in patience and remain steadfast.' He said: 'Being patient upon the Obligations.'

key_terms.الْفَرَائِضِ: The Obligations (plural of Faridah, referring to mandatory religious duties)
key_terms.صَابِرُوا: Excel in patience / Make others patient

ai.seo_question: What does the Quranic command to be patient refer to in Shia interpretation?
ai.summary: In this concise narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) offers a specific exegetical lens to the triad of commands in Surah Al Imran 3:200, defining 'Asbiru' (be patient) as steadfastness in performing obligatory duties (Fara'id). This interpretation grounds the abstract virtue of sabr in concrete ritual practice, a view supported by Shia scholars who emphasize that true patience is manifested through the consistent fulfillment of religious obligations amidst worldly distractions.
